_comment: Two directions are documented per task_type below. incoming_request = what the external server POSTs to /api/v1/bot/execute-task to enqueue a job (envelope shape: {task_type, machine_name, data}; machine_name is optional). outgoing_result_response = what THIS bot POSTs back to the server once the job finishes, built by _call_record_result() in services/queue_service.py — marked with _direction so it's unambiguous which way each block flows.

incoming_request._direction: INCOMING — server sends this to the bot

requirements.description: 50 double-sided 3" x 4" PVC name tags with one hole and plastic sleeves

outgoing_result_response._direction: OUTGOING — bot POSTs this back to the server once the job finishes
outgoing_result_response.posted_to: the literal BACK_URL_RECORD_RESULT from the request above (http://localhost:8000/api/v1/quotation/job/result) — create_estimate is the only task_type NOT redirected to a customer-history endpoint
outgoing_result_response._note: Matches the receiving endpoint's actual schema exactly, as given: queue_id, success, summary_file_name, summary_file_url, error_message, estimate_totals, estimate_id — nothing else. file/status/attempt metadata that the other two task types' payloads carry (task_type, machine_name, tenant_id, status, attempt, max_attempts, will_retry, storage_key, etc.) is deliberately NOT sent here since this endpoint doesn't expect it (see the else-branch in _call_record_result for those). Values (summary_file_name/url, estimate_totals) are from a real run, queue_id 6a1416213a96293ce1db0552. estimate_id is null because this was a brand-new estimate creation (no estimate_id in the incoming request) — run_estimate_flow never captures a newly-created estimate's own ID.

incoming_request._direction: INCOMING — server sends this to the bot

outgoing_result_response._direction: OUTGOING — bot POSTs this back to the server once the job finishes
outgoing_result_response.posted_to: derived from BACK_URL_RECORD_RESULT: same scheme/host/port, path replaced with /api/v1/customer-history/job/export-result (see http://localhost:8000/api/v1/customer-history/job/export-result) — see _derive_result_url() in services/queue_service.py
outgoing_result_response.content_type: multipart/form-data — NOT application/json. See _post_form_with_file() in services/queue_service.py.
outgoing_result_response._note: No public copy of the CSV is ever created — the bot uploads the local temp download's actual bytes as a file attachment (field name 'file') on success, then deletes that temp file once the callback POST completes (success or failure), see _cleanup_local_result_file() in services/queue_service.py. On failure (or if the local file is missing for any reason), this falls back to a plain application/json POST with just queue_id/success/error_message/history_file_name since there's no file to attach and no URL to send.

file.content: <raw CSV bytes read from the file at result['history_file_local_path']>

incoming_request._direction: INCOMING — server sends this to the bot

outgoing_result_response._direction: OUTGOING — bot POSTs this back to the server once the job finishes
outgoing_result_response.posted_to: derived from BACK_URL_RECORD_RESULT: same scheme/host/port, path replaced with /api/v1/customer-history/job/invoice-result (see http://localhost:8000/api/v1/customer-history/job/invoice-result) — see _derive_result_url() in services/queue_service.py
outgoing_result_response._note: Trimmed to queue_id/success/error_message plus invoice_id and the scraped record itself — no JSON file is written to disk any more, the scraped result is only logger.info()'d for local debugging and sent straight through in this callback ({invoice_id, requirements, direct_charges}). requirements is shaped exactly like create_estimate's incoming 'requirements' (job_method/description/stock_search/size/sides/quantity/job_charges/product/stock_color/location/job_comment/unit_per_side/price) so the receiving server can treat a Digital Color, Multi-Part, etc. entry here the same way it treats one it originally sent in a create_estimate request — see _to_requirements_format() in etimate_history/invoice_history_lookup.py. A Multi-Part job's requirements entry additionally carries an 'other_charges' key (Charges-Only parts folded in), right after its own job_charges.

requirements.description: 2,000 stickers printed and delivered to Pier 48 San Francisco, CA 94158
